listen_ip.description: IP address for the DNS server to listen on (e.g., 127.0.0.1, ::, or 0.0.0.0 for all).

port.description: UDP port to listen on for incoming DNS queries (standard DNS port is 53).

domain.description: Top-level domain (TLD) subdomain you control and will use for tunneling (e.g., dns.example.org).

secret.description: Shared secret (≥20 characters) used to authenticate clients. Keep this secure and identical on all clients.

max_tunnels.description: Maximum number of simultaneous client tunnels. Adjust based on RAM/CPU limits.

idle_timeout.description: Seconds of inactivity after which an inactive tunnel is closed.

compress.description: Enable payload compression to reduce bandwidth usage. Requires client-side support.

max_pktsize.description: Maximum UDP packet size (in bytes) used for DNS tunneling (must be between 512 and 4096).

verbose.description: Enable detailed runtime logging (use sparingly in production due to log volume).

interface.description: Network interface (e.g., eth0) to bind DNS queries to (optional).

chroot.description: Chroot jail directory (e.g., /var/chroot/iodine) for security isolation (optional).

user.description: Unix username to drop privileges to after initialization (e.g., 'nobody', 'iodine').

group.description: Unix group to drop privileges to after initialization (e.g., 'nogroup', 'iodine').

upstream_resolver.description: Upstream DNS resolver for queries not related to tunnel setup (e.g., '8.8.8.8' or '8.8.8.8#53').

ttl.description: DNS record TTL (seconds) for A/TXT responses (recommended: 300–600).

allow_ips.description: List of client IPs/CIDRs allowed to connect. Empty list means all IPs allowed.

deny_ips.description: List of client IPs/CIDRs explicitly denied access (e.g., known malicious IPs).

record_type.description: DNS record type used for the main data channel (TXT is standard and most compatible).

status_record_type.description: DNS record type used for status/heartbeat queries (TXT or A recommended).

redirect.description: IP address to return in A responses for non-tunnel DNS queries (useful for bypassing captive portals).

server.description: Main server configuration block for iodine DNS tunneling.
